title: hours of service requirements
objectives: State examples of off-duty and on-duty time
Explain the difference between on-duty driving and on-duty-not-driving time
Explain how long you can drive before you must take a break
List the minimum requirements for filling in a RODS (Record of Duty Status)
Identify the hours of service requirements in other jurisdictions

sections.title: National Safety Code and on/off-duty definitions
points: The NSC sets minimum safety standards for commercial vehicles, drivers and carriers in Canada.
NSC applies to commercial vehicles over 5,000 kg GVW, Passenger Transportation Act vehicles, and vehicles seating 10-plus passengers plus driver.
Hours of service rules limit driving time because fatigued drivers are more likely to crash.
On-duty time includes driving, inspecting, servicing, loading/unloading, checking loads, and waiting at scales or customs.
Travelling as a passenger to start driving is on duty if the carrier requested it and you lacked eight consecutive hours off beforehand.
Off-duty time is any time you are not on duty, including time in a sleeper berth.
Ferry time is not on-duty time unless you are working, such as a bus driver selling tickets.
mustKnow: The NSC program includes commercial vehicles licensed with a GVW more than 5,000 kg.
It also covers vehicles under the Passenger Transportation Act and commercial vehicles seating 10 or more passengers plus the driver.
A sleeper berth does not include the back seat of a bus or a reclining seat.

check.q: The National Safety Code program includes commercial vehicles licensed with a GVW of more than what weight?
check.explanation: The NSC includes commercial vehicles licensed with a GVW more than 5,000 kg.

check.q: Which of the following counts as off-duty time?
choices: Waiting at a weigh scale for a load check
check.explanation: Off-duty time includes time spent in a sleeper berth; the other activities are on-duty time.

sections.title: Daily limits and the three-point check
points: A day is a 24-hour period beginning at the hour designated by the carrier.
Three-point daily check: at least 10 hours off duty, no more than 13 hours driving, no driving after 14 hours on duty.
Off-duty time beyond the mandatory eight consecutive hours may be split into blocks of 30 minutes or more.
Daily off-duty time must include at least two hours outside the eight-consecutive-hour block.
All drivers must take 24 consecutive hours off duty every 14 days.
You can put in 14 hours of on-duty time without doing any driving at all.
mustKnow: Minimum 10 hours of off-duty time must be taken every day.
Maximum 13 hours of driving in a day.
No driving after 14 hours on duty in a day.
Off-duty blocks other than the eight consecutive hours must be 30 minutes or more, including at least two hours outside the eight-hour block.
All drivers must take 24 consecutive hours off duty every 14 days.

check.q: What is the maximum number of hours you are allowed to drive in a day?
check.explanation: You are allowed to drive a maximum of 13 hours in a day.

check.q: How often must every driver take 24 consecutive hours of off-duty time, regardless of cycle?
check.explanation: All drivers must take 24 consecutive hours off duty every 14 days.

sections.title: Work shift, cycles and resets
points: A work shift is the elapsed time between two off-duty periods of at least eight consecutive hours.
No driving after 16 hours of elapsed time until you take eight consecutive hours off duty.
Every off-duty period of eight consecutive hours or more resets the work shift.
Cycle 1: no driving after 70 on-duty hours in seven days.
Cycle 2: no driving after 120 hours in 14 days, with 24 consecutive hours off before accumulating 70 on-duty hours.
The cycle start time stays the same; you must reset a cycle to change it.
A peace officer can order you (not the vehicle) out of service for exceeding cycle on-duty hours.
mustKnow: No driving after 16 hours of elapsed time in a work shift.
Cycle 1: maximum 70 on-duty hours in seven days.
Cycle 2: maximum 120 hours in 14 days, plus at least 24 consecutive hours off duty before accumulating 70 on-duty hours.
Reset Cycle 1 with 36 consecutive hours off duty; reset Cycle 2 with 72 consecutive hours off duty.

check.q: How many consecutive hours off duty are required to reset Cycle 1?
check.explanation: Taking 36 consecutive hours off duty resets Cycle 1; 72 hours resets Cycle 2.

check.q: Under Cycle 2, you must not drive after completing how many on-duty hours in 14 days?
check.explanation: Cycle 2 drivers must not drive after completing 120 hours in 14 days.

sections.title: Deferral, sleeper berth and personal use
points: You may defer up to two hours of the daily 10-hour off-duty requirement to the next day.
Deferred hours cannot come from the eight consecutive off-duty hours and must be added to the next day's eight consecutive hours.
Mark deferral as 'Day 1' and 'Day 2' on your RODS.
Single drivers may split off-duty time into two sleeper-berth periods: neither under two hours, totalling at least 10 hours.
Team drivers may split into two periods: neither under four hours, totalling at least eight hours, with total off-duty time at least 10 hours.
Personal use is off duty only if unloaded, no trailer, maximum 75 km a day, odometer recorded, not out of service.
mustKnow: Off-duty time may be deferred by up to two hours to the next day, with 'Day 1' and 'Day 2' noted on the RODS.
Single-driver sleeper berth split: two periods, neither less than two hours, total off-duty at least 10 hours.
Team-driver sleeper berth split: two periods, neither less than four hours, totalling at least eight hours, with total off-duty time at least 10 hours.
Personal use maximum is 75 km a day with the vehicle unloaded and not towing a trailer.

check.q: What is the maximum distance you may drive a commercial vehicle each day under the personal use exemption?
check.explanation: Personal use is limited to a maximum of 75 km a day with the vehicle unloaded and not towing a trailer.

check.q: By how many hours may you defer your daily 10-hour off-duty requirement to the next day?
check.explanation: You may reduce the 10-hour off-duty requirement by up to two hours, added to the next day's eight consecutive hours.

sections.title: ELDs, RODS, local exemption and other jurisdictions
points: ELDs are required as of August 1st, 2023; they automatically record driving time, which may not be shortened.
Drivers must verify entries, certify their RODS daily, and use only one ELD at a time.
If an ELD malfunctions, notify the carrier when parked; the carrier has 14 days to repair or replace it.
Keep RODS for the current day plus the previous 14 days (24 for oilwell service hours) and submit to your carrier within 20 days.
Within 160 km of home terminal: exempt from RODS and ELDs if returning daily for 10 consecutive hours off; carrier keeps records.
North of the 60th parallel: maximum 15 hours driving, no driving after 18 hours on duty; Cycle 1 is 80 hours in seven days.
In the U.S.: 11 hours driving after 10 hours off, no driving beyond the 14th hour, 60 hours/7 days or 70 hours/8 days, 34-hour restart.
mustKnow: ELDs are required as of August 1st, 2023; a malfunctioning ELD must be repaired or replaced within 14 days.
Keep copies of your RODS for the present day and the previous 14 days (24 days for oilwell service vehicle hours); submit RODS and supporting records to your carrier within 20 days.
160 km exemption: operate within 160 km of the home terminal, return daily for 10 consecutive hours off duty, no deferral; carrier keeps records at least 6 months.
North of 60: maximum 15 hours driving, no driving after 18 hours on duty; Cycle 1 is 80 hours in 7 days, Cycle 2 is 120 hours in 14 days with 24 hours off before 80 on-duty hours.
U.S. rules: 11 hours driving after 10 hours off duty, no driving beyond the 14th hour, 60 hours in 7 days or 70 hours in 8 days, restart after at least 34 consecutive hours off.

check.q: Within how many days must you submit your RODS and supporting records to your carrier?
check.explanation: You must submit your RODS and all supporting records to your carrier within 20 days.

check.q: When driving in the U.S., how many hours may you drive after taking 10 hours of off-duty time?
check.explanation: U.S. rules allow 11 hours of driving after 10 hours of off-duty time.

summary: Daily three-point check: at least 10 hours off duty, maximum 13 hours driving, no driving after 14 hours on duty.
No driving after 16 hours of elapsed work-shift time; eight consecutive hours off resets the shift.
Cycle 1 is 70 hours/7 days (36-hour reset); Cycle 2 is 120 hours/14 days with 24 hours off before 70 hours (72-hour reset).
ELDs are mandatory since August 1st, 2023; keep RODS for 14 days and submit to your carrier within 20 days.
Rules differ north of 60 and in the U.S. — learn each jurisdiction's requirements before you enter.
